text_map.central_idea: The speaker addresses Autumn as a person and praises its ripeness, its unhurried ease and its own music. Even while celebrating this fullness, the poem quietly admits that the season is ending, through the dying day, the stubble fields, the mourning gnats and the gathering swallows.
text_map.speaker_or_narrator: An admiring observer who speaks directly to Autumn throughout (apostrophe). He describes the season first as a ripening force, then as a figure at rest among the harvest, and finally as the owner of an evening music. He also consoles Autumn about the lost songs of Spring.

devices.function: Closes on sound and on a hint of migration.

text_map.central_idea: On a desolate winter evening that feels like the funeral of the dying century, a speaker who feels as lifeless as the land hears a frail old thrush pour out a joyful song. Since nothing he can see justifies such joy, he wonders whether the bird knows of some hope that he himself cannot share.
text_map.speaker_or_narrator: A first-person speaker, alone outdoors at dusk, leaning on a coppice gate after everyone else has gone indoors. He reads the landscape through his own lack of feeling and only tentatively guesses at what the bird's song means.

devices.quote: The weakening eye of day
devices.function: Makes the setting sun seem like a failing, dying being and sets up the mood of decline.

devices.quote: Like strings from broken lyres
devices.function: Compares the vine stems to the strings of ruined instruments, so the world seems to have lost its music.

devices.quote: His crypt the cloudy canopy
devices.function: Turns the landscape into the corpse of the century lying in its tomb, so the scene reads as a funeral.

devices.quote: Was shrunken hard and dry
devices.function: Shows the life force of nature as withered and sterile.

devices.quote: In a full-hearted evensong
devices.function: Sets an overflowing song against the dry, deathly world of the first two stanzas.

devices.quote: Had chosen thus to fling his soul
devices.function: Words of will and force ('chosen', 'fling') make the song a deliberate, generous act.

devices.quote: At once a voice outburst among
devices.function: Marks the poem's turn from desolation to an unexpected sign of life.

devices.quote: An aged thrush, frail, gaunt, and small
devices.function: The bird's frail body is set beside its unlimited joy, and the bird as a whole is set beside the fervourless speaker.

devices.quote: Upon the growing gloom
devices.function: The repeated g sounds stress how heavy the darkness is that the song is thrown against.

text_map.central_idea: An adult narrator recalls his boyhood in a drab, decaying Dublin street, where his growing infatuation with Mangan's sister turns an ordinary girl into an object of nearly religious devotion. The feeling transfigures his grim surroundings, though he could not understand it at the time.
text_map.speaker_or_narrator: A first-person retrospective narrator, an adult looking back on himself as a boy. He reports the boy's feelings closely and lets the adult's judgment show through words like "foolish" and through his admissions of what he did not understand then.

text_map.central_idea: On a bright Sunday in the public gardens, Miss Brill delights in her fur, the band, and the crowd she watches. The close narration also lets the reader see a loneliness she will not name. Her pleasure comes from overhearing and watching other people, and her scorn for the 'odd, silent' bench-sitters quietly points back at her.
text_map.speaker_or_narrator: A third-person narrator who stays very close to Miss Brill and often slips into her own thoughts and exclamations (free indirect discourse). Her guesses, judgments and self-corrections come through without comment from the narrator.

text_map.central_idea: Through epigrams that turn conventional values upside down, the opening conversation mocks the upper-class idea of marriage, morality and good manners. Algernon preaches rules that he excuses himself from, Lane deflects his master with deadpan wit, and Jack's answers about his name and his county hint that he is hiding something.
text_map.speaker_or_narrator: There is no narrator. This is dramatic dialogue between Algernon, his manservant Lane and his friend Jack, with stage directions that sometimes give information the dialogue does not, such as labeling the man announced as Ernest with the name JACK.
